behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: One pass over the training split only. For each training session (ordered item list) and each consecutive pair (a,b) in that session, N[a,b] += 1. ideas.coupling_path: training transitions -> popularity-adjusted successor barycentres b_i -> prefix behaviour centroid b_bar_p -> one-sigma critical-confusion set -> surgical target set S* -> geodesic two-means on {b_i : i in S*} -> Gromov-delta cut certificate -> level-L code rewrite. The behaviour signal decides WHICH items may move and the curved operator decides WHETHER the move is structurally sound and margin-improving; removing behaviour empties or randomises S*, removing curvature changes every distance, mean and defect in the same chain, and in both cases the rewritten code table differs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the deepest-level loss is driven by genuine top-two confusion on high-mass prefixes rather than by noise, then a precision-first edit that touches only the successor items of one-sigma-indistinguishable prefixes will (i) move a small fraction of the catalogue, well below the previous one third, (ii) leave the validation L1 negative hit rate unchanged or better rather than degrading it, (iii) lower the deepest-code conditional entropy of the touched prefixes, and (iv) raise Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Observed directly from the outputs of the single frozen Stage-3 run; if the moved fraction is small and recall does not move, the confusion hypothesis is falsified and the negative result is recorded with numbers.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: At quantization/SID-construction time, after the frozen 3000-epoch Stage 2 and before the frozen 150-epoch Stage 3, acting only on the level-L code assignment; also inside the split proposal, where the two-way assignment and the centroid updates are geodesic rather than linear.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with fixed negative curvature kappa = -1: exponential and logarithmic maps at the origin, Poincare distance d_P, Karcher/Frechet means, and the Gromov product (x|y)_o with the induced delta-hyperbolicity defect of a cluster.
ideas.key_change: Successor transitions from the training split produce a Poincare successor barycentre per item and a prefix-conditional deepest-code confusion table; a critical-confusion set is extracted from that table by a one-sigma counting band; a curved split of the confusable code is proposed on the successor barycentres of only the successor items of critical prefixes; and the split is written into the SID table only if a Gromov-delta cut certificate holds on the split and the Poincare margin of every triggering critical prefix strictly increases.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The SID edit reads only A_ij and pop_j from the training split and only parameters of the frozen Stage-2 model, which itself was trained on the training split. The critical set, the certificate and the margin rule are all functions of training counts and frozen centroids, so no validation or test interaction can influence which code an item receives. The validation L1 negative hit rate is computed after the SID table is frozen and is written to the log as a diagnostic only; it is never compared against a threshold inside the mechanism and never reverts a move.
ideas.motivation: The previous round executed a certificate-valid but coverage-first move set and edited about one third of the catalogue; the deep level of the SID therefore stopped being a stable refinement of the prefix and the validation L1 negative hit rate fell. The real failure mode of a generative recommender is not a badly partitioned catalogue, it is a small set of high-mass prefixes whose top-two deepest codes are statistically indistinguishable, so that the frozen Stage-3 model cannot commit to the correct continuation. Only those prefixes are worth editing, and only if the edit widens a geodesic decision margin.
ideas.novelty: Unlike the earlier successor-Frechet codebook updates, per-level curvature control and behaviour-ranked radial assignment, this mechanism never touches the codebook, the curvature, the encoder or the training of Stage 2. It is a post-Stage-2 relabelling that changes only level L, and its new element is an ADMISSION TEST that a move must pass on top of the certificate: the move must touch a critical-confusion pair, defined by a one-Poisson-sigma band on the training-split top-two deepest-code counts for a frozen prefix, together with the condition that the competitor is the geodesically nearest competing code as seen from the prefix behaviour centroid. A move that merely preserves the hyperbolic tree structure is rejected unless it demonstrably sharpens a margin the frozen Stage-3 context actually has to resolve.
ideas.observables: moved fraction of the 24556 training items; validation L1 negative hit rate before and after; per-item deepest-code conditional entropy before and after, mass-weighted and per touched prefix; the number of critical pairs found and the number of admitted versus rejected moves in each round; and finally Stage-3 test_recall@10 of the single trained run.

ideas.safeguards: clamp ||x|| <= 1 - 1e-5 before every arcosh and arctanh and add 1e-8 inside the arcosh argument; Karcher step clamped to 0.5 and stopped after 5 iterations; reject any move with |U| < 3 or |S*\U| < 3, or with rad(X) = 0, or with delta_S = 0 (nothing to certify); deterministic tie-breaking by lowest code index everywhere; assert that the multiset of prefixes is bit-identical before and after the edit; cap the number of splits by the number of merge-admissible codes so the level-L vocabulary cannot grow without bound; if the critical set is empty or every move is rejected, write the unchanged table and record a zero-move result rather than relaxing any threshold.
ideas.spec_equations:
d_P(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2)))
  log_0(x) = arctanh(||x||) * x/||x||,  exp_0(y) = tanh(||y||) * y/||y||
  bary({x_i, a_i}) = exp_0( sum_i a_i log_0(x_i) ),  sum_i a_i = 1
  Karcher: m <- exp_m( sum_i a_i log_m(x_i) ), 5 iterations, step clamped to 0.5
  w_ij = (A_ij/n_i)/sqrt(pop_j) normalised;  b_i = bary({z_j}, {w_ij})
  b_bar_p = bary({b_i : i in P_p}, {n_i / sum n})
  N(p,k) += 1 for each training transition i->j with p(i)=p, k_L(j)=k; n_p = sum_k N(p,k)
  critical(p) = [N(p,k1)-N(p,k2) <= sqrt(N(p,k1))] and [k2 = argmin_{k != k1, N(p,k)>0} d_P(b_bar_p, c_k)]
  M0(p) = d_P(b_bar_p, c_k2) - d_P(b_bar_p, c_k1);  M1(p) = d_P(b_bar_p, m'') - d_P(b_bar_p, m')
  (x|y)_o = 0.5*(d_P(o,x) + d_P(o,y) - d_P(x,y))
  delta_S = 0.5 * max_{x,y,z in S} max(0, (x|y)_o - min((x|z)_o,(z|y)_o))
  rad(X) = median_{i in X} d_P(b_i, m_X)
  pseudocode:
    for round in 1..3:
      N := confusion_table(current level-L codes, A)
      C := [(p,k1,k2,M0) for p if critical(p)]
      if C empty: break
      Sstar := union over C of successors(p) restricted to k_L = k1(p)
      for each k1 in keys(Sstar):
        (m', m'', U) := geodesic_2means({b_i : i in Sstar}, b_bar of triggering p)
        if not (S-a and S-b and S-c): reject, continue
        if not all(M1(p) > M0(p) for triggering p): reject, continue
        commit k_L(j) := k1' for j in U, k1'' for j in Sstar\U
      assert hash(k_1..k_{L-1}) unchanged
    report moved_fraction, val_L1_negative_hit_rate(before, after), H(K_L|p)(before, after)
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the training-split transition counts A_ij, training popularity pop_j, the frozen Stage-2 level-L centroids c_k, the frozen item latents z_i, and the frozen prefixes p(i). Outputs are a rewritten level-L code for a subset of items, an unchanged prefix table (asserted by hash), a per-round move log with admitted and rejected counts, and the three mandatory diagnostics.

specification.text:
Notation. L RQ levels; item i has code (k_1(i),...,k_L(i)) with prefix p(i) = (k_1(i),...,k_{L-1}(i)) frozen and bit-identical throughout. c_k in B^d is the frozen Stage-2 level-L centroid of code k, curvature kappa = -1, Poincare distance d_P, ball radius 1. z_i is the frozen Stage-2 item latent used by the deepest level. All statistics come from the training split only.
1. Successor geodesic barycentre. With directed training counts A_ij, rowsum n_i = sum_j A_ij, training popularity pop_j:
   w_ij = (A_ij / n_i) / sqrt(pop_j), renormalised to sum_j w_ij = 1 over j with A_ij > 0;
   b_i = exp_0( sum_j w_ij * log_0(z_j) ), and b_i = z_i when n_i = 0.
2. Prefix behaviour centroid. For prefix p with item set P_p, b_bar_p = exp_0( sum_{i in P_p} (n_i / sum_{i' in P_p} n_{i'}) * log_0(b_i) ).
3. Prefix confusion table. For every training transition i -> j, increment N(p(i), k_L(j)). n_p = sum_k N(p,k). k1(p) = argmax, k2(p) = second largest in N.
4. Critical set (THE ADDITIONAL PRECISION CONDITION). p is critical iff
   (C1) N(p,k1) - N(p,k2) <= sqrt(N(p,k1))   [one-Poisson-sigma band; derived from the counts, sigma = 1 is the standard one-standard-error rule, not a swept constant]
   (C2) k2 in argmin_{k != k1, N(p,k) > 0} d_P(b_bar_p, c_k)   [nearest competing code under the frozen Stage-2 geometry]
   Base margin M0(p) = d_P(b_bar_p, c_k2) - d_P(b_bar_p, c_k1).
5. Surgical move target. S* = { j : j is a successor under some critical p } intersect { j : k_L(j) = k1 }. Only items in S* may change their code; every other item keeps its code.
6. Curved split proposal for code k1. m = Frechet mean of {b_i : k_L(i)=k1} (Karcher iteration, 5 steps). U = { i in S* : d_P(b_i, b_bar_p) < d_P(b_i, m) }. Seed m_a = Frechet mean of U, m_b = Frechet mean of S*\U; run 3 alternating rounds of assignment by d_P and Frechet-mean update. Split k1 into k1' = the part whose centroid is geodesically nearer b_bar_p and k1'' = the other part, with centroids m' and m''.
7. Certificate, split side (necessary, inherited in spirit from the previous round). With the metric induced by {b_i : i in S*}, Gromov product (x|y)_o = 0.5*(d_P(o,x)+d_P(o,y)-d_P(x,y)), o the ball origin, and cluster defect
   delta_S = 0.5 * max_{x,y,z in S*} max(0, (x|y)_o - min((x|z)_o, (z|y)_o))   (deterministic index-stride sampling of triples when |S*| > 200),
the split is admissible iff
   (S-a) d_P(m', m'') >= 2*max(rad(k1'), rad(k1'')), rad(X) = median_{i in X} d_P(b_i, m_X);
   (S-b) delta_S - delta_{S after split} >= 0.5 * delta_S;
   (S-c) cross-transition mass between the two parts <= median_{i in S*} sum_{j in S*} A_ij.
8. Certificate, merge side. Two level-L codes ka, kb may be merged only if both are members of no critical pair, d_P(m_ka, m_kb) <= min(rad(ka), rad(kb)), the merged cluster defect is <= max(delta_ka, delta_kb), and the directed transition mass between them exceeds the within-median of clause (S-c). Merges exist to keep the level-L vocabulary size from growing and to make the both-off ablations well defined; a merge is executed only when the split budget has been exhausted.
9. Execution rule. A split is written only if clauses (S-a),(S-b),(S-c) hold AND the margin rule M1(p) > M0(p) holds for every critical p that triggered it, with M1(p) = d_P(b_bar_p, m'') - d_P(b_bar_p, m'). Recompute the confusion table from step 3 and repeat, at most 3 rounds, stopping earlier when no move is admitted. Three is a fixed documented default, not a tuned value.
10. Mandatory reporting (recorded, never used as a gate): moved fraction |{i : k_L changed}| / 24556; validation L1 negative hit rate before and after the edit; per-item deepest-code conditional entropy H(K_L | p) computed on training transitions, before and after, reported mass-weighted and for every touched prefix.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: M identically zero. Wbar empty, R_{p,k} empty, b(i) has no candidate, the mechanism produces exactly zero moves and the SID table equals the frozen Stage-2 table; the geometry code still runs but every accept test fails at the destination step.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full run above: behaviour affinity picks b(i) and sets h_{p,b}; the Poincare Busemann test and the geodesic surprisal sign test gate the move.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace d_H by the Euclidean norm, xi_{p,k} by the normalised Euclidean mean direction, and B_{p,k}(x) by the linear functional <x, xi_{p,k}>, with h_{p,k} the median of that functional over R_{p,k}. The horoball becomes a flat half-space and Delta_i a squared Euclidean distance difference; the same accept rule then selects a different move set.
ideas.behavior_computation: For every training session, take each consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) with u_t != u_{t+1}, count once per user into M, using only items present in the training split; pop from the same split. Then Wbar[k->j] = sum_{i in child k} M[i,j]/(pop_k pop_j), and the per-item affinity to a sibling cell is sum_{j in child k} (M[i,j]+M[j,i])/sqrt(pop_i pop_j). Only the stage-2 training split file is opened.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transition counts from consecutive interactions, popularity-normalised and aggregated to deepest-cell successor flow. Training split only.
ideas.cost_estimate: Essentially zero training cost. Stage 2 unchanged at 3000 epochs (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 72000 steps); Stage 3 unchanged at the frozen 150 epochs with unchanged vocabulary size. One offline pass between stages: per parent O(|S_p| * K * d) sibling affinities plus O(|S_p| * |Ch_p|) Busemann evaluations, total about 24556 * 256 * 64 ~= 4.0e8 multiply-adds plus one 1-NN graph, i.e. well under one CPU-minute; peak memory |S_p| * K floats because parents are streamed. Per-step added cost at the frozen scale: 0 flops on any of the 72000 Stage-2 steps and 0 on any Stage-3 step.
ideas.coupling_equation: accept(i) = [|child a| >= 2] AND [i not a cut vertex of G_a] AND [B_{p,b(i)}(x_i) - h_{p,b(i)} >= 0] AND [d_H(x_i,m_{p,b(i)})^2 - d_H(x_i,m_{p,a})^2 <= 0], with b(i) = argmax_k sum_{j in child k} (M[i,j]+M[j,i])/sqrt(pop_i pop_j) and h_{p,k} = median_{j : Wbar[k->j]>0} B_{p,k}(x_j).
ideas.coupling_path: training transitions -> per-parent successor flow -> destination child b(i) and behaviour-implied horosphere height h_{p,b} -> Busemann test D_i = B_{p,b}(x_i) - h_{p,b} -> joint with geodesic surprisal Delta_i against frozen child anchors -> accept/refuse -> new k_L -> Stage-3 labels. Behaviour fixes the destination and the height; curvature fixes the coordinate system and the test; neither half can decide acceptance alone.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the deepest code is where behaviour coherence is destroyed while the prefix context is still usable, a horosphere-gated transplant will lower per-item deepest-code conditional entropy for moved items, leave the validation L1 negative hit rate exactly unchanged, and push Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Worth keeping if moved fraction is roughly 1-10%, entropy drops for moved items, and Recall@10 improves; refuted if a few percent move and Recall@10 is flat or worse, meaning the deepest level is not where the Stage-3 loss concentrates.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: After Stage-2 training is frozen and before Stage-3 training begins, as a discrete reassignment of the level-L index only; it acts on the SID table, on no weight.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of radius 1, fixed constant negative curvature K=-1; exp_0 injection with data-derived scale s; geodesic distance d_H = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))); Busemann function B_{p,k}(x) = log((1-||x||^2)/(2||x-xi_{p,k}||^2)) toward the ideal boundary point xi_{p,k}; horoball membership D_i >= 0; Riemannian (Frechet) child anchors by 8 fixed gradient steps.
ideas.key_change: Every item gets one hyperbolic Busemann height coordinate toward each sibling child cell's ideal boundary point; the destination child is chosen by training-split directed successor affinity, the item moves only if it lies inside that child's behaviour-implied horoball AND the move does not raise its geodesic distance to the child's frozen Stage-2 anchor relative to its current one, and only if a two-sided structural certificate holds.
ideas.leakage_boundary: M, pop, s, S0, child anchors, horosphere heights and the accept set are functions of the stage-2 training split and of the frozen Stage-2 weights (which saw only that split). Validation interactions are read only after the SID table is frozen, and only to print the L1 negative hit rate before/after; they never enter b(i), D_i, Delta_i or the certificate. Test interactions are never read before the single Stage-3 test evaluation.
ideas.motivation: The frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE assigns the deepest code k_L by residual nearest-neighbour in Euclidean space, so two items a user actually moves between in one session can sit under different deepest tokens while their L-1 prefixes agree. Stage 3 can only exploit a deepest-code improvement if the prefix it is conditioned on still points at that token; the previous round moved a third of the catalogue on a certificate that was necessary but not sufficient, and the validation L1 negative hit rate caught it. This idea repairs only the deepest level, and only where a curved membership test and a curved no-harm test agree, so the move set is small and every move is one the frozen prefix context can support.
ideas.novelty: Prior rounds in this programme used (i) successor-weighted Frechet updates of codebook vectors, (ii) a per-level curvature scalar set by prefix-transition hardness, (iii) behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment with per-item curvature from context entropy. This mechanism uses none of those objects: it uses the IDEAL BOUNDARY of the Poincare ball (Busemann functions, horoballs), a purely negatively-curved construct with no Euclidean analogue that is neither a radius, nor a curvature scalar, nor a codebook mean; it acts after Stage 2 as a discrete transplant of the deepest code only, leaving levels 1..L-1 bit-identical; and its precision ingredient is a sign test on a geodesic surprisal DIFFERENCE, which contains no tunable constant.
ideas.observables: (1) moved fraction |moved|/N, expected a few percent; (2) validation L1 negative hit rate, the fraction of (validation positive, fixed-seed validation negative) pairs whose level-1 tokens coincide, before and after - predicted bit-identical because k_1 is untouched, so it is a regression guard proving the earlier failure mode cannot recur; (3) per-item deepest-code conditional entropy H_i = -sum_k q_ik log q_ik over sibling children with q_ik proportional to the behaviour affinity, reported for moved items and for all items, before and after; (4) training-split successor rank of each item's own deepest code, before and after; (5) Stage-3 test_recall@10.
risks: The move set may be too small to shift Recall@10 (the deepest token carries only part of the generation loss). The monotone assumption behind Delta (Stage 3's prefix-to-child preference tracks geodesic distance to m_{p,k}) may fail, rejecting the moves that would help. Single-child parents, or parents whose children hold only singletons, contribute nothing. The 1-NN cut-vertex test is noisy on sparse low-popularity behaviour graphs. A pure label transplant with no codebook change can interact badly with an already-overfit Stage-3 last-token head.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||x_i|| <= 1-1e-3 at injection and after every Frechet step; clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-8; guard ||m_{p,k}|| < 1e-6 with the highest-pop member direction fallback; guard 1-||x||^2 > 0 in the Busemann logarithm via the clip; skip parents with |Ch_p| < 2 or with fewer than 2 items in every child; empty R_{p,k} leaves h_{p,k} undefined and forces refusal for that child; deterministic tie-breaks (smallest code index, then smallest item id) for bit-reproducibility; assert levels 1..L-1 unchanged for all N items and the Stage-3 vocabulary set size unchanged before running Stage 3; assert no validation or test id appears in M.
ideas.spec_equations: 1) s = median_{ordered pairs in S0} ||z_i - z_j||/2; x_i = tanh(||z_i||/s)*(z_i/||z_i||), clipped to ||x_i|| <= 1-1e-3. 2) d_H(x,y) = arcosh(clamp(1 + 2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2)), 1+1e-8, inf)). 3) m_{p,k} = FrechetMean_{d_H}({x_i : i in S_p, k_L(i)=k}) with 8 Riemannian steps of size 1/8. 4) xi_{p,k} = m_{p,k}/||m_{p,k}||. 5) B_{p,k}(x) = log((1-||x||^2)/(2||x-xi_{p,k}||^2)). 6) Wbar[k->j] = sum_{i in child k} M[i,j]/(pop_k pop_j); h_{p,k} = median_{j in R_{p,k}} B_{p,k}(x_j). 7) b(i) = argmax_k sum_{j in child k} (M[i,j]+M[j,i])/sqrt(pop_i pop_j). 8) accept iff certificate(a,i,p) and D_i >= 0 and Delta_i <= 0, with D_i = B_{p,b}(x_i) - h_{p,b} and Delta_i = d_H(x_i,m_{p,b})^2 - d_H(x_i,m_{p,a})^2. 9) new k_L(i) = b(i) if accepted else k_L(i); one synchronous pass; revert the highest-pop mover if a child code of p would be emptied.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training split sessions; frozen Stage-2 encoder latents z_i for all training items; the frozen SID table (k_1..k_L) and level-L code vectors c_L[k]; the frozen codebook size K. Outputs: a new deepest-code column k_L' for a subset of training items (all other levels bit-identical), plus a report record {moved_fraction, L1_negative_hit_rate_before, L1_negative_hit_rate_after, deepest_code_entropy_before, deepest_code_entropy_after, cut_vertex_refusals, horoball_refusals, surprisal_refusals}.

specification.text:
Notation. N=24556 training items; frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE with L levels and per-level codebook size K (K_L children per parent); z_i the frozen encoder latent; SID(i)=(k_1..k_L); parent p(i)=(k_1..k_{L-1}); S_p={i: p(i)=p}; Ch_p={k_L(i): i in S_p}. Only k_L may change.
Step 0 (behaviour, training split). M[i,j] = number of consecutive training-split pairs (u_t=i, u_{t+1}=j) over all training sessions, deduplicated per user so a repeated pair counts once per user. pop_i = number of training users who interacted with i.
Step 1 (curved embedding, fixed curvature). Deterministic 4096-item training sample S0 (the 4096 smallest training item ids). s = median over ordered pairs of S0 of ||z_i - z_j||_2 / 2. x_i = exp_0(z_i/s) = tanh(||z_i/s||) * (z_i/s)/||z_i/s|| in the Poincare ball of radius 1, constant curvature K=-1; clip ||x_i|| <= 1-1e-3. d_H(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). s and the clip are derived, not tuned.
Step 2 (child anchors, ideal boundary). For each parent p and k in Ch_p: m_{p,k} = Frechet mean of {x_i : i in S_p, k_L(i)=k} under d_H, by exactly 8 Riemannian gradient steps of size 1/8 from the Riemannian centroid (fixed, deterministic). xi_{p,k} = m_{p,k}/||m_{p,k}||; if ||m_{p,k}|| < 1e-6 fall back to x_j/||x_j|| for the highest-pop member j.
Step 3 (Busemann / horosphere). B_{p,k}(x) = log((1-||x||^2)/(2||x-xi_{p,k}||^2)). Only differences of B are used, so its additive normalisation is irrelevant.
Step 4 (behaviour-implied horosphere height, derived). Wbar[k->j] = (sum_{i in child k} M[i,j])/(pop_k pop_j); R_{p,k} = { j not in S_p : Wbar[k->j] > 0 }; h_{p,k} = median over j in R_{p,k} of B_{p,k}(x_j). Measured, no free constant.
Step 5 (candidate for item i in child a). b(i) = argmax over k in Ch_p, k != a of sum_{j in child k} (M[i,j]+M[j,i])/sqrt(pop_i pop_j), ties by smallest code index. D_i = B_{p,b}(x_i) - h_{p,b} (>=0: inside b's behaviour-implied horoball). Delta_i = d_H(x_i,m_{p,b})^2 - d_H(x_i,m_{p,a})^2 (<=0: geodesic surprisal not increased).
Step 6 (necessary two-sided certificate). Split side: |child a| >= 2 and i is not a cut vertex of the within-cell 1-NN behaviour graph G_a (nodes = members of child a, each node joined to its top-1 behaviour neighbour inside the cell, affinity as above, ties by item id); this keeps each deepest code's behaviour connectivity, which is what the frozen prefix was trained against. Merge side: b(i) already exists in Ch_p (no new code is created) and no child code of p is emptied by the batch.
Step 7 (sufficiency gate, the new precision condition). Accept iff certificate passes AND D_i >= 0 AND Delta_i <= 0. Justification with no tuned constant: m_{p,k} are the frozen Stage-2 level-L code vectors carried into the ball by an isometry, so the frozen quantiser's preference for token k given prefix p is monotone decreasing in d_H(x_i, m_{p,k}); a move with Delta_i > 0 makes the item strictly less reachable by the frozen prefix-to-token map, so any behaviour-coherence gain cannot be realised at generation time. Delta_i <= 0 is the sign of a difference, hence the unique constant-free cut, and it is measured entirely from the training split and the frozen Stage-2 geometry.
Step 8 (application). Exactly one synchronous pass per parent (no iteration: a fixed point is not guaranteed and would need a stopping constant). Accepted moves apply simultaneously; if the batch empties a child code of p, revert the single highest-pop moved-out item so the Stage-3 vocabulary set is unchanged. Report moved fraction, validation L1 negative hit rate before/after, per-item deepest-code conditional entropy before/after.

ideas.title: Ideal-boundary horosphere transplant of the deepest RQ code, gated by a constant-free geodesic surprisal test against the frozen Stage-2 child anchors

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Neighbourhoods are emptied (N32(i) = ∅), so y_i = x_i, all weights are set to zero so T is replaced by the curved-nearest-cell indicator, and the H-gate and u-condition are disabled (Hmed := −∞). The result is a pure curved nearest-centroid reassignment under the same δ_loc margin and the same capacity cap. The switch exists and is unit-tested on a 200-item dry run which must produce a different move set; no arm is trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full pathway above, run once: frozen Stage-2 (3000 epochs, four cards) → the one-pass relabel with δ_G-derived curvature and training-demand gating → frozen Stage-3 (150 epochs) → test_recall@10. This single run is the candidate; any diagnostic that would normally be used to pick a setting is reported only.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The c = 0 branch is taken: exp_0 and log_0 become the identity, d_P becomes the Euclidean chord distance, Karcher means become arithmetic weighted means, and δ_loc(i) becomes the Euclidean chordal image of a δ_G tangent step. The behaviour graph, W, δ_G-as-a-number, the H-gate, the u-condition and the cap are all unchanged. The switch exists and is unit-tested; no arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training split only. For each training session (ordered item list) and each consecutive pair (a,b) in that session, N[a,b] += 1. W_ij = N_ij + N_ji. m_i = column sum of the training next-item event counts (equivalently Σ_j N_ji plus session-terminal targets, counted exactly as Stage 3's target construction does on the training split). Derived quantities: per-prefix demand p(c|π) = Σ_{i∈cell(π,c)} m_i / Σ_{i:π_i=π} m_i, per-prefix deepest-token entropy H(π) = −Σ_c p(c|π) log p(c|π), per-item cell mass u(π,c) = (Σ_{i∈cell(π,c)} m_i)/(|cell(π,c)|·Σ_{i:π_i=π} m_i), median gate Hmed over prefixes with at least two non-empty cells, and the hop metric on the giant component of A.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions (symmetrised to W_ij = N_ij + N_ji) from ordered training sessions, plus the derived training next-item demand m_i (number of training next-item events whose target is i).
ideas.cost_estimate: Zero added cost inside training: 0 extra FLOPs on each of the 72,000 Stage-2 steps (24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs) and 0 on every Stage-3 step, because nothing is added to either loop — the mechanism is a one-shot post-Stage-2 construction whose output is a new deepest-token table. One-time precompute ≈ 2–4 CPU-minutes and <1 GB: 2048 BFS over ≈24.5k nodes and a few 10^5 edges (≈10^9 edge traversals, the dominant term), 262,144 quadruple evaluations (constant time each), 24,556 exp maps plus 24,556×20 Karcher retractions, a few thousand cell means, and a sparse T over at most 32 neighbours per item. Peak memory: 2048² float32 = 16 MB for the distance matrix, plus 24,556×64 float32 for the points. No GPU time, no retraining.
ideas.coupling_equation:
accept(i → c′) iff
  H(π_i) > Hmed
  and u(π_i,c′) > u(π_i,c_L(i))
  and T(i,c′) > T(i,c_L(i)),  T(i,cell) = Σ_{j∈cell} W_ij·exp(−(d_P(y_i,y_j;κ) − dmin_i)) / Σ_{j:W_ij>0} W_ij·exp(−(d_P(y_i,y_j;κ) − dmin_i))
  and d_P(y_i, m_{π_i,c′}; κ) + δ_loc(i) < d_P(y_i, m_{π_i,c_L(i)}; κ)
  and |cell(π_i,c′)| < cap(π_i) = max_c |cell(π_i,c)| at frozen Stage 2,
with the behaviour term W_ij and the curved term d_P(·;κ) appearing multiplicatively inside the same statistic and the same decision.
ideas.coupling_path: TRAIN sessions → symme trised counts W → unweighted transition graph → BFS hop metric → measured four-point defect δ_G → curvature c = 1/max(δ_G,1) → exp map of the encoder embedding into the ball → weighted Karcher smoothing whose neighbourhood and weights are W → curved cell centroids → the transfer statistic T and the margin d_P + δ_loc → accept/reject of the deepest-code move → new SIDs → frozen Stage 3. Removing behaviour deletes the neighbourhood, the weights, δ_G (hence κ) and the demand gate, so the computation becomes plain Euclidean-to-ball nearest-centroid; removing curvature deletes d_P, the exp map and the Karcher mean, so the same move set is decided by chordal distances and the tolerance collapses to a Euclidean δ. Either way the accepted move set changes, which is why the coupling is real rather than decorative.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping only if three things hold in the single run: the moved fraction is materially smaller than the previous one third while still non-trivial (a few percent), the deepest-token conditional entropy falls under the entropy-eligible prefixes (the moves land where uncertainty was, not in already-well-predicted regions), and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065. Observation is by direct comparison of the recorded before/after tables and the single test number; no arm is trained, so the case must be carried by the both-on run plus the pre-registered diagnostics.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: At SID construction after the frozen Stage-2 quantization: the encoder embedding is mapped into the ball, the behaviour smoothing is a curved mean, cell centroids are curved means, and the accept/reject margin of each discrete deepest-code move is a curved distance increment. Nothing is added to the Stage-2 or Stage-3 training loops.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré ball of constant negative curvature κ = −c² with c = 1/max(δ_G, 1.0) (δ_G in hop units, so c has units 1/hop), with exp_0^κ(v) = tanh(c‖v‖)·v/(c‖v‖), d_P(x,y) = (1/c)·arcosh(1 + 2c²‖x−y‖²/((1−c²‖x‖²)(1−c²‖y‖²))), Riemannian Karcher means under d_P, and a radius-dependent local resolution δ_loc(i) = d_P(exp_0^κ(v_i), exp_0^κ(v_i + δ_G·n_i)) with n_i a fixed unit vector orthogonal to v_i. Curvature is fixed, not trained. Distances carry the standard factor-2 convention relative to tangent norms (d_P(0, exp_0(v)) = 2‖v‖); every inequality below uses the same d_P, so the factor never has to be calibrated.
ideas.key_change: After the frozen Stage-2 run, each training item gets a hyperbolic point (exp map of its encoder embedding under a curvature fixed by the measured δ_G of the training transition graph), smoothed by a weighted Karcher mean over its training transition neighbours; each (prefix, deepest-code) cell gets a curved centroid. An item's deepest code is then reassigned inside its own prefix only if five inequalities hold simultaneously: a hyperbolic margin of one local δ, a transition-share advantage, a demand advantage, an entropy-eligible prefix, and a capacity cap taken from the frozen Stage-2 cell sizes. Stage 3 then runs unchanged on the relabelled SIDs.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Every input to the move predicate — N, W, m_i, H(π), Hmed, u, the 2048-item BFS sample, the 16 anchors, δ_G, κ, s, and the frozen Stage-2 cell sizes — is computed from the training split and frozen Stage-2 artifacts only. Validation is touched only after the relabel, read-only, to produce the before/after diagnostics; it never enters a threshold, a sort key or a stopping rule, and because levels 1..L-1 are bit-identical the validation L1 negative hit rate is required to come out exactly unchanged (asserted in code as a falsification check, not used to choose anything). Test is untouched until the single frozen Stage-3 evaluation. No early stopping, no selection among variants, no seed repetition.
ideas.motivation: The frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE resolves the first L-1 tokens well but leaves the deepest token carrying almost no behavioural information: items whose training next-item demand differs sharply sit in the same (prefix, level-L) cell, so Stage 3 must memorise the tail of the SID instead of reading it off the tree. The earlier certificate round tried to fix this by moving one third of the catalogue on a predicate that was necessary but not sufficient, which redistributed the deepest codes without changing what Stage 3 actually has to emit and raised the validation L1 negative hit rate. This idea replaces coverage-first movement with a two-sided certificate whose tolerance is a *measured* hyperbolicity of the training transition graph and whose admissibility is additionally gated by training-split next-item demand, so that a move is only accepted when it changes the token Stage 3 must produce in a region where that token is genuinely uncertain.
ideas.novelty: The occupied slots in this repository's history are: curved codebook update (Poincaré–Fréchet successor codebook), per-level curvature from a prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), radial behaviour-ranked assignment (BRad-RQ), Lorentz successor profiles, behaviour cones, geodesic boosts, MoE branch curvature, fibre mixtures. This idea touches none of them: both codebooks and levels 1..L-1 are frozen and bit-identical, the curvature is a single fixed value derived from the measured Gromov four-point defect of the training transition graph (not per level, not trained, not a radial coordinate), and the novel object is that the *same measured δ is re-expressed as a radius-dependent local hyperbolic resolution* δ_loc(i) which becomes the margin a discrete move must beat. The second novelty is the admissibility condition itself: a per-prefix deepest-token entropy gate and a per-item next-item-mass condition, both computed on the training split, which separate "satisfies the tree certificate" from "reduces what Stage 3 has to guess".
ideas.observables: Moved fraction of the 24,556 training items (must be far below the previous one third). Per-prefix deepest-token entropy H(π) before and after, and per-item deepest-code conditional entropy H(π_i) before and after, reported as distributions. Validation L1 negative hit rate before and after (must be exactly equal, by bit-identity of levels 1..L-1, and is asserted). Validation (L−1)-prefix negative hit rate before and after (free to change; expected to fall). Number of distinct (prefix, code) cells and the maximum cell size. Stage-3 test_recall@10 for the single frozen run, judged against 0.065.
risks: The training transition graph may be far from tree-like, giving a large δ_G, a small κ and a geometry almost indistinguishable from Euclidean; the behaviour graph may be too sparse to give most items a non-empty 32-neighbourhood, so almost nothing is admissible and the mechanism is inert; hyperbolic Karcher means shrink points toward the origin, which shortens all distances and could make the margin test too permissive; the median entropy gate could select prefixes that are high-entropy only because their cells are tiny; Stage 3 may be nearly insensitive to the deepest token (short SID, strong memorisation), in which case even a correct relabel cannot move recall; and the cap, anchored to frozen Stage-2 cell sizes, may block exactly the moves that matter when one cell is already dominant.
ideas.safeguards: arcosh argument clamped to ≥ 1 + 1e-12; ball coordinates clamped to ‖x‖ ≤ (1 − 1e-5)/c; a c < 1e-6 branch runs the Euclidean formulas to avoid division by c; δ_G = 0 is floored to 1 hop so κ stays finite and the margin becomes strict rather than infinite; log-sum-exp with the per-item minimum distance prevents exp underflow when d_P is large; items with an empty neighbourhood never move (T undefined → reject); unreachable pairs in the BFS metric are dropped from the four-point sample and clipped on the anchor-vector path; Karcher iterations have a fixed count with a divergence check on the step norm (break if it grows twice in a row) and return the initial point on failure; a source cell may never fall below one item and a target cell may never exceed the frozen max cell size, so no empty prefix code and no concentration; deterministic tie-breaking by (score, item index, code index) makes the relabel reproducible; a pre-registered assertion that the validation L1 negative hit rate is bitwise identical before and after relabels is raised as a hard failure if violated; the moved-fraction ceiling is an output, never a target, so no constant is chosen to hit a coverage number.
ideas.spec_equations:
Pseudocode, everything once, seed 20261031.
  for (a,b) in consecutive pairs of each TRAIN session: N[a,b] += 1
  W = N + N.T ; A = (W > 0) ; G = giant weak component of A
  S = 2048 nodes of G sampled deterministically ; D_S = BFS hop distances (inf if unreachable)
  Q = 262144 quadruples from S (seed) ; δ_G = max_Q (s1 − s2)/2, s = descending sort of {d_ab+d_cd, d_ac+d_bd, d_ad+d_bc}
  c = 1/max(δ_G, 1.0) ; κ = −c²
  A16 = farthest-point sample of 16 nodes of G seeded at argmax degree ; D_i = hop distances to A16, inf clipped to the max finite value
  zc = z − mean(z) ; s_scale = median‖D_i‖ / median‖zc_i‖
  v_i = s_scale·zc_i ; x_i = tanh(c‖v_i‖)·v_i / (c‖v_i‖)    [v_i = 0 → x_i = 0]
  ω_ij = W_ij / max_{k∈N32(i)} W_ik , ω_ii = 1 , N32 = top-32 neighbours by W (ties by index)
  y_i = Karcher({x_j, ω_ij}, init x_i, 20 steps of step 1.0): grad = −2Σ_j ω_ij log_{y}(x_j)/Σ_j ω_ij ; y ← exp_y(−grad)
  for each cell: m_cell = Karcher({y_j}, uniform, init = mean)
  dmin_i = min_{j:W_ij>0} d_P(y_i,y_j) ; T(i,cell) = Σ_{j∈cell} W_ij e^{−(d_P−dmin_i)} / Σ_j W_ij e^{−(d_P−dmin_i)}   [log-sum-exp form]
  v_i^t = s_scale·zc_i ; n_i = normalize(any fixed vector ⊥ v_i) ; δ_loc(i) = d_P(exp_0(v_i^t), exp_0(v_i^t + δ_G·n_i))
  Hmed = median{H(π) : π has ≥ 2 non-empty cells}
  cand = all (i, c′) with π(c′) = π_i, c′ ≠ c_L(i)
  keep cand if H(π_i) > Hmed, u(π_i,c′) > u(π_i,c_L(i)), |cell(π_i,c′)| < cap(π_i),
              T(i,c′) > T(i,c_L(i)),
              d_P(y_i, m_{π_i,c′}) + δ_loc(i) < d_P(y_i, m_{π_i,c_L(i)})
  sort by (T(i,c′) − T(i,c_L(i))) descending, then (i, c′) ascending
  accept greedily if the source cell keeps ≥ 1 item and the target cell is under cap; one pass, no re-scoring
  write c_L′(i) ; assert c_1..c_{L-1} unchanged for every item and both codebooks unchanged (hash the tensors before/after)
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the encoder embedding z_i of every training item (dimension d, e.g. 64), the frozen level assignments (c_1..c_L)(i), the two/three codebooks, the training session sequences, the codebook size K at level L, the number of levels L, the fixed seed 20261031. Outputs: a new deepest-level assignment c_L′(i) for a subset of the 24,556 training items (levels 1..L-1 and all codebook tensors bit-identical, verified by a hash assertion); and a diagnostic bundle containing the moved fraction, per-prefix and per-item deepest-code conditional entropy before/after, validation L1 and (L−1)-prefix negative hit rates before/after, cell-count and max-cell-size before/after, δ_G, c, and the number of candidates rejected by each of the five conditions.

specification.text:
All quantities below are computed once after Stage 2, from the training split only, with a fixed seed 20261031; no gradient flows into SID construction; Stage 3 is then the single frozen 150-epoch run.
(1) Symmetrised transition matrix W_ij = N_ij + N_ji from ordered training sessions; unweighted graph A = 1[W>0], giant weak component G.
(2) Hop metric: BFS from a deterministic 2048-item sample S of G; δ_G = max over 262144 sampled quadruples (a,b,c,d) of (largest − second largest)/2 of {d_ab+d_cd, d_ac+d_bd, d_ad+d_bc}. Curvature c = 1/max(δ_G, 1.0), κ = −c².
(3) 16 farthest-point-sampled anchors (seeded at the max-degree node); tangent vector v_i = s·(z_i − mean z) with s = median‖D_i‖ / median‖z_i − mean z‖ (D_i = the 16 hop distances). x_i = exp_0^κ(v_i) = tanh(c‖v_i‖)·v_i/(c‖v_i‖).
(4) y_i = Riemannian weighted Karcher mean (20 fixed steps, step 1.0, retraction by exp) of {x_j : j ∈ {i} ∪ N32(i)} with ω_ii = 1 and ω_ij = W_ij/max_k W_ik.
(5) Cell = (π_i, c_L(i)) with π_i = (c_1..c_{L-1})(i); m_cell = Karcher mean of {y_j : cell(j)=cell}.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors.
